name: GravityOps Forum – Lite
author: BrightLeaf Digital

sections.description:
GravityOps Forum turns Gravity Forms forms and entries into a working forum with categories, forums, topics, and replies, while keeping entries as the canonical data source.

With custom rewrite rules enabled, forum routes use their own page context and return HTTP 404 for missing or inaccessible content. Trashed and spam entries stay hidden. Login and registration forms redirect after submission, and the hub meta description can be set in Configuration.

Paid features include:
* Template Hijacking: Override default plugin templates within your own WordPress theme.
* Nested Forums: Create sub-categories and multi-level forum hierarchies.
* Additional Fields: Map additional Gravity Forms fields to display in topic and reply content.
* Gravity Forms Feeds: Use native feeds to automate topic/reply creation with full conditional logic support.
* Follow Content & Email Alerts: Enable users to follow topics, forums, and other users with automatic email notifications for new activity.
* Advanced Role Mapping: Map WordPress roles to specific forum access sets.
* Forum Boards: Group forums into logical boards.

Community Help

For how-to questions and examples of what others have built, visit the GravityOps Help community.

If you opened a support thread on WordPress.org, continue that conversation there. The community is an additional place for help and ideas.

External services

Your forum content and member data stay on your site.

The plugin connects to outside services only in these cases:

  • GravityOps product catalog. When an administrator uses the WordPress admin (or shortly afterwards, through WP-Cron), the shared GravityOps library downloads the GravityOps product catalog (names, versions, icons, links and announcements) from brightleafdigital.io, at most about twice a day. The request sends no personal data or site content; like any web request, it reveals your server’s IP address.
  • Newsletter signup. Only if you choose to subscribe to GravityOps Weekly, the email address you enter is sent to brightleafdigital.io.
  • Feedback prompts. Only if you choose to answer the short GravityOps survey or open the review prompt, your answers, or the plugin and version being reviewed, are sent to brightleafdigital.io.
  • Support access. Only if you grant BrightLeaf Digital support access, TrustedLogin creates a temporary login and notifies BrightLeaf Digital through TrustedLogin and brightleafdigital.io.
  • Freemius. Licensing and updates for the premium version run through Freemius. In the free version, Freemius receives information only if you opt in when activating the plugin: your name and email address, your site’s URL, your WordPress, PHP and plugin versions, and plugin events such as activation and deactivation. You can skip the opt-in and the plugin works the same.

BrightLeaf Digital: Privacy Policy. TrustedLogin: Authorized User Terms, Privacy Policy. Freemius: Terms, Privacy Policy.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0 | Nov 10, 2026

  • Added a setting for the forum hub’s meta description. Leave it empty to keep the automatic description.
  • Forum pages now load with the correct page context, and missing or private content returns a proper “not found” page. Trashed and spam posts are hidden everywhere, and topics only load under the forum they belong to.
  • Profile pages have their own title and are kept out of search engines.
  • Fixed login and registration forms sometimes showing the default Gravity Forms message instead of the forum’s confirmation.
  • New how-to questions now point to the GravityOps Help community.
  • Added an External services section to this readme describing when the plugin connects to outside services.
  • Updated the GravityOps shared library: the GravityOps dashboard now gets its product list, categories, links and announcements from BrightLeaf Digital’s signed online catalog, so new tools appear without a plugin update. Free versions offer an optional GravityOps Weekly newsletter signup, seasonal offers can appear on the plugin’s settings screen, and updating from the dashboard keeps a network-activated plugin network-active.

1.1.4 | Oct 28, 2026

  • Forums can require a higher access set to start topics than to view or reply. Leave Start Topics as Same as Forum Access to keep the previous behavior. Administrators can still start topics.
  • Rich-text posts no longer get an extra line break after every block. Plain text still gets paragraph formatting, and editing a post keeps allowed HTML.
  • When custom rewrite rules are on, links inside shortcodes use the same pretty URL as the rest of the forum. Old query-string forum and topic links redirect to that URL.
  • Pretty forum pages now have their own titles, descriptions, and canonical URLs. Yoast SEO and Rank Math receive the same metadata, and public forums and topics are included in their sitemaps. Draft, private, hidden, and anonymous-blocked forums stay out and are not indexed.
  • Appearance menus can add Forum index, Profile, and Logout links. Logout returns to the forum hub and shows a confirmation.
  • Updated how the Freemius SDK is packaged. The SDK version is unchanged.

1.1.3 | Oct 25, 2026

  • Improved additional-field display across older and newer Gravity Forms versions.
  • Updated the GravityOps shared library with clearer premium update requirements, more consistent dashboard navigation and review prompts, corrected Code Snippet Manager links, and more reliable admin table display.

1.1.2 | Oct 11, 2026

  • Fixed the forum not registering with the GravityOps dashboard in distributed builds.
  • Forum form buttons now keep their branded styling on Gravity Forms 3.0.
  • Updated Freemius SDK to the latest version.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.1.
  • Updated the GravityOps shared library to 2.0.11, bringing a consistent Feeds screen across the suite, more reliable feed activation toggles and feed links, the Docs tab placed before Help, dashboard links that open in a new tab, and updated third-party components.

1.1.1 | Aug 3, 2026

  • GravityOps now asks for one short suite-wide survey instead of one survey per plugin, using a compact invitation and a dedicated dashboard form.
  • Closing a survey or review prompt now saves “not interested” immediately without reloading the page.
  • Fixed release packaging so distributed builds include the correct plugin files and dependencies.
